subject: Control-plane stability regressions after private upgrade — OrthoTech impact
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya@orthotech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden errors after private cluster upgrade

Hi Marissa —

We started seeing a spike in 502/503s across our private deployment this morning after the agent-side upgrade you rolled out late yesterday (11/17). Failures started around 03:40 UTC and are intermittent but persistent — roughly 2–5% of inference requests fail with a control-plane handshake timeout.

Our SREs gathered logs and a trace bundle, attaching a compressed dump (agent-dump-20261118.tar.gz). The attached includes a bunch of TLS handshake rejects and a short period where KV cache reads were returning stale sequence numbers. Impact so far: degraded user-facing latency and occasional failed requests for our elective scheduling service.

Can you confirm whether Redwood pushed any controlplane config changes or new kernel changes for privileged agents overnight? We need an ETA on a fix and whether you can roll us back to the previous agent variant.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Singh
Head of Platform Reliability, OrthoTech Solutions

Priya — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We're taking this seriously.

Short summary of immediate next steps from our side:
- Triage call in 30 minutes (I set up a bridge at 15:35 PST) — link to follow in separate calendar invite.
- Aditya + infra will validate agent variant and control-plane config; if rollback is necessary we'll coordinate maintenance window with you.
- As a mitigation, we can pin your cluster to the previous agent build and route new requests to a fallback controlplane tier while we investigate. This will introduce a small failover latency bump (~50–100ms) but should eliminate the handshake timeouts.

Can you confirm whether you saw any node reboots around 03:30–04:00 UTC and share the SRE runbook output? We'll review the logs you attached now.

Marissa — quick technical notes (internal):

- I pulled the uploaded trace bundle. There are repeated TLS connection resets originating from agent instances that were scheduled with the new 1.12.0-priv build. Handshake failure pattern lines up with an optimization we enabled for abbreviated re-handshake on long-lived streams.
- The control-plane also logged a small window (~7m) of slow KV cache writes that coincided (03:38–03:45 UTC). Noting correlation, not causation yet.
- Temp mitigation options: 1) Roll back agents to 1.11.4 across OrthoTech's pool (fastest); 2) Enable legacy handshake path in config (config toggle, no agent restart required) — we can push toggle to your private controlplane in ~15–20 minutes if you approve.

I'll be on the bridge. If we go with config toggle, runtime footprint unchanged; rollback is safest for regressions but will require a coordinated rolling restart of agents (we'll script it for low blast radius).

- aditya

Thanks team — we've confirmed no node reboots and no infrastructure changes on our side in the window you identified. The SRE bundle includes per-agent TLS stacks and the handshake traces.

We prefer a config toggle first to avoid restarts during our peak window. Please proceed with toggling the legacy handshake path and confirm expected timeline. We'll monitor after the change.

Separately, our product team has rolled back any risky deploys that touch the scheduling surface to reduce surface area. Current impact estimate: ~3% request failure rate, elevated latencies for affected endpoints.

—Priya

Subject: Post-incident follow-up: timeline, root-cause hypothesis, and next steps

Priya — thank you for working with us through the bridge and for the detailed traces. Below is our interim post-incident summary and immediate next steps. We'll publish a fuller postmortem doc to the shared Drive and JIRA ticket INF-4821 within 48 hours.

Interim timeline (UTC):
- 2026-11-17 23:50 UTC: Canary push of agent 1.12.0-priv across private customers (orchestrated roll).
- 2026-11-18 03:38–03:45 UTC: Spike of TLS handshake resets and KV cache slow writes observed (matches OrthoTech traces).
- 2026-11-18 15:05 PST: OrthoTech reports 502/503 spike; bridge established.
- 2026-11-18 15:35 PST: Config toggle to legacy handshake path applied to OrthoTech private controlplane. Immediate reduction in handshake rejects observed.

Root-cause hypothesis (interim):
- A new abbreviated re-handshake optimization in agent 1.12.0-priv interacts poorly with certain TLS stacks under long-lived stream patterns in OrthoTech's environment, leading to handshake resets and temporary control-plane KV pressure.

Action items and timelines:
- [<48h] Full artifact collection and deterministic reproduction in internal test harness (Aditya).
- [72h] Validation run of a targeted rollback to 1.11.4 in a non-prod subset and automated canary checks (Marissa + Infra).
- [7d] Release candidate with handshake fix + extended canary plan and shared rollback runbook.
- Redwood will propose a customer credit based on measured downtime and error-rate impact; Ben has started the HubSpot ticket for follow-up.

Attachments included in thread: agent-dump-20261118.tar.gz, controlplane-timeline-orthotech.csv, privnet-config-snapshot-1118.txt

Please let us know if you'd like an on-site runbook review or a dedicated postmortem session with your platform team. We'll keep this thread updated as artifacts and the postmortem doc are published to JIRA/Drive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
